headline: Maui Board of Ethics

meeting.summary: The Maui Board of Ethics approved two advisory opinions finding no conflicts and formed a working group to review Charter section 10-4.4.
meeting.recap: The Maui Board of Ethics met on July 8, 2026.[[0:00:30]] No one signed up to give public testimony.[[0:04:04]] The executive director reported 25 informal advisory opinions from May 13 through July 7, 2026.[[0:04:23]] A committee will hear the board's priorities on July 28, 2026, including its nepotism law and lobbyist rules.[[0:06:06]] The board voted unanimously that a housing department employee may run a private energy consulting business, if he keeps it separate from his county work.[[0:15:03]] The board voted unanimously that a Maui Planning Commission member's job as a union organizer does not inherently conflict with that role.[[0:28:40]] A working group's report on County Charter section 10-4.3 was shared for information only.[[0:29:41]] The board voted to form a permitted interaction group (a small group of members) to review Charter section 10-4.4.[[0:32:54]] The board voted to dissolve its working group on gift guidelines.[[0:34:26]] The board voted to form a new working group on gift guidelines.[[0:35:33]] The board went into executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[0:37:15]] The next meeting is August 12, 2026, at 12:30.[[0:40:28]]
decided: The board approved an advisory opinion that a housing department employee's private consulting business is not incompatible with his county job, with conditions.
The board dissolved the gift guidelines working group it set up in May 2025.
The board formed a new working group to recommend updated gift guidelines for county departments and employees.
The board voted in public to ratify its executive session decision on the financial disclosure statement.
meeting.next: The executive director hopes to decide on hiring a paralegal or legal secretary in the next couple of weeks. The office plans an online training video in addition to in-person trainings. The housing department employee will receive the advisory opinion in writing. The chair asked the executive director to include general guidance from the ethics office in the union organizer's advisory opinion.
